I am a PhD Candidate in the Population Biology Graduate Group and co-advised by Rachael Bay and Eric Sanford. My research examines the eco-evolutionary consequences of the poleward range shift of the owl limpet (*Lottia gigantea*). My work combines field surveys, laboratory experiments, and genomics to understand how selection pressures differ across the range with respect to life history traits. More broadly, I am interested in how spatial and temporal genetic variation interacts with the environment for adaptive and/or range-shift potential. Beyond my research, I am passionate about increasing access to research and graduate school through mentorship. In my free time I enjoy baking, reading, ice skating, and making elaborate tea services for loved ones.
